answer: Short‑term memory (STM) is a temporary storage system that receives information from sensory memory and holds it for about 15–30 seconds. It can hold roughly 7 ± 2 items (though more recent work suggests a capacity of 4 ± 1). Information in STM can be moved to long‑term memory through rehearsal—either active rehearsal (repeating the material) or elaborative rehearsal (linking it to existing knowledge). If the material is not rehearsed, it is discarded.

Short‑term memory (STM) is a temporary storage system that processes incoming sensory information. It holds information for about 15–30 seconds, similar to the contents displayed on a computer screen. Information in STM can be moved to long‑term memory through rehearsal—active rehearsal (repeating the material) or elaborative rehearsal (linking it to existing knowledge). STM has a limited capacity, typically around 7 ± 2 items (or 4 ± 1 in more recent studies).
